summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +15.5%; weakest: Oats -18.0%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.98% (-28 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-28 bp); 2s10s curve +37 bp (+0 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.98% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.81 (+0.4% in a month, +3.6% YTD). USD/BRL 5.436 (+4.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.642 (-0.9%); USD/MXN 18.90 (+4.8%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.6% in a month (+12.8% YTD); VIX 18.7. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 103.94 $/bbl (+17.6% in a month), Brent 113.10, ULSD 4.673 $/gal (+3.7%), natural gas 2.88 (-14.7%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -1.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.3%, Hang Seng -5.4%, yuan +0.9% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 12 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (36%); S&P GSCI +2.6% in a month; gold -5.3%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
